1. Core Clinical Tension: An asymptomatic 52-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B cirrhosis admitted for portal vein thrombosis evaluation is found to have an incidental mixed ground-glass pulmonary nodule. Despite being HIV-negative with normal CD4 counts and normal inflammatory markers, tissue sequencing proved opportunistic Talaromyces marneffei linked to consumption of bamboo rats.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint is set after admission physical examination, baseline routine laboratory tests, and the initial chest CT identifying the right upper lobe ground-glass lesion, stopping strictly before invasive lung biopsy, histopathology stains, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing.
3. Differential Distinctions: A solitary mixed ground-glass opacity in an older cirrhotic patient with normal inflammatory markers strongly simulates primary adenocarcinoma of the lung. Co-detected EBV/gammaherpesvirus 4 reads represent latent carriage, excluded by negative IgM serology. Metagenomic NGS and history of bamboo rat consumption pinpointed localized pulmonary talaromycosis.
case_prompt:
A 52-year-old man born and raised in Anhui, China, was admitted for evaluation and treatment of portal vein thrombosis discovered one year earlier. His past medical history was notable for chronic hepatitis B diagnosed in 2008 maintained continuously on nucleoside analogue therapy, and splenectomy performed in 2016 following gastrointestinal bleeding secondary to ruptured esophageal and gastric varices. Recent abdominal ultrasound demonstrated absent significant blood flow in the main and right portal veins, reduced flow velocity in the left portal vein branch, and dilation of the splenic and superior mesenteric veins. He had no fever, cough, sputum production, chest tightness, shortness of breath, abdominal distension, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or melena. He denied smoking or alcohol use and had no history of recent travel. During the recent Spring Festival, he consumed bamboo rats.

On physical examination, body temperature was 36.5°C, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 83 beats per minute, and respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute. There was no superficial lymphadenopathy, cutaneous jaundice, or scleral icterus. Abdominal examination showed a surgical splenectomy scar, an impalpable liver edge beneath the right costal margin, an absent spleen, and no palmar erythema or spider angiomas.

Triage laboratory testing showed an HIV-negative status with a normal CD4+ T-cell count (532.89 cells/µL). AST, GGT, ALP, and total bilirubin were slightly elevated; albumin and platelet count were mildly decreased (Child-Pugh score 5, Class A). Procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, absolute neutrophil count, serum galactomannan assay, and (1,3)-beta-D-glucan assay were all within normal limits. A chest computed tomography (CT) scan revealed a mixed ground-glass lesion in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe of the lung, raising concern for inflammation or neoplasm.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: An asymptomatic mixed ground-glass nodule in the right upper lobe in an older adult without elevated inflammatory markers (CRP and PCT normal) raised strong suspicion for early-stage lung neoplasm; however, lung biopsy showed focal granulomatous inflammation and NGS proved fungal infection rather than malignancy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: After admission, a chest CT scan revealed a mixed ground glass lesion in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe of the lung, with potential for inflammation or tumor (Figure 1A).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing detected human gammaherpesvirus 4 sequence reads alongside the fungal pathogen, but viral capsid antigen and early antigen IgM were negative, indicating latent viral persistence rather than active pulmonary infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: NGS of the biopsy confirmed lung infection with TM (n = 51 reads) and human gammaherpes virus 4 (n = 17 reads) 2 days later (Figure 2). We further examined the EB virus and found that both the capsid antigen and early antigen IgM were negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In the setting of bamboo rat ingestion, metagenomic next-generation sequencing of the lung biopsy specimen confirmed Talaromyces marneffei infection with 51 specific sequence reads, with targeted voriconazole therapy producing complete radiographic resolution of the lesion.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: During the 2023 Spring Festival, patients consumed bamboo rats.
